shortDescription: Parcel locker company InPost, recently taken over by a consortium led by FedEx NYSE:FDX and Advent International, aims to invest heavily to expand several-fold over the next five years, Chief Executive Rafal Brzoska said.($1 = 0.9103 euros)($1 = 4.0552 zlotys)

children: Parcel locker company InPost, recently taken over by a consortium led by FedEx
and Advent International, aims to invest heavily to expand several-fold over the next five years, Chief Executive Rafal Brzoska said.
The company, which operates across nine countries including Poland, has one of Europe's largest networks of automated parcel lockers
Its delisting from Euronext Amsterdam following its takeover earlier this year has freed the company up, Brzoska told Reuters in an interview

"We are preparing for every scenario - organic growth, M&A, and entry into new markets. The reason we need this private setup is to be able to finance our expansion through debt, and to do so more aggressively than we have in the past," Brzoska said

"It also allows us to operate with fewer constraints regarding quarter-on-quarter investor expectations; you simply cannot pursue rapid growth while simultaneously adhering to a strict regime of improving results every single quarter," he added
InPost's revenue rose more than 34% to 14.7 billion zlotys  ($3.62 billion) in 2025, but net profit fell nearly 58% to 526 million zlotys
"...if the company were to grow three, four, or perhaps even five times over — that would undoubtedly be a worthy ambition," Brzoska said
Brzoska said InPost planned to enter Ireland in 2027 and deploy more than 1,000 parcel lockers within two years. It is also interested in partnerships with local companies
"We are in the midst of highly advanced integrations with several players that will provide us with access to foreign markets," he said without giving details

title: InPost aims for rapid expansion after FedEx-Advent buyout, CEO says
